claim: Define a procedure $\mathsf{Wirtinger}(D,a_0)$ on a finite planar code $D$ for one oriented knot and a designated under-arc $a_0$ as follows. First check all incidence, valence, branch-pairing, crossing over/under, edge-orientation, and one-component conditions in the code. For each pair of rational line segments in the drawing certificate, compute the determinant of their direction vectors. If it is nonzero, solve the two-coordinate linear intersection equations and check whether the solution lies on both closed segments. If the determinant is zero, test collinearity and overlap by exact rational determinant and endpoint-order comparisons. Accept an intersection only when it is a shared declared bend or crossing vertex with the recorded incidence, and at a crossing verify that the two branch direction vectors have nonzero determinant. Reject self-intersections and all unrecorded intersections. If any check fails, return `invalid-input`. Otherwise traverse the oriented knot once starting at $a_0$, label the maximal under-arcs $a_1,\ldots,a_m$, and introduce one symbol $x_i$ for the positive meridian of each $a_i$. For each crossing $v$, read its oriented over-tangent and positive in-plane normal. Let $a_s$ be the under-side from which that normal points and $a_t$ the side toward which it points, and read the over-arc $a_o$. Append exactly the relator $x_o^{-1}x_sx_ox_t^{-1}$. Equivalently, if the incoming under-tangent follows that normal, append $x_o^{-1}x_{\rm in}x_ox_{\rm out}^{-1}$; otherwise append $x_ox_{\rm in}x_o^{-1}x_{\rm out}^{-1}$. The orientation of a positive meridian is fixed locally by requiring the knot tangent followed by the normal-disk orientation to give the ambient orientation. Once a complement basepoint and basing paths to the meridians are fixed, interpret $x_i$ as the corresponding based positive meridian. Return the finite group presentation with generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and this one relator per crossing.

Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$ uses the product Euclidean norm induced by the chosen trivialization. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. claim: Assume full AC. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link, let $F$ be a compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$, and put $X=S^3\setminus L$. For each component $K_i$, let $\mu_i$ be the positive meridian, oriented as the boundary of a small normal disk so that a positive tangent to $K_i$ followed by the disk's positive basis gives the ambient orientation. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the free abelian group on $[\mu_1],\ldots,[\mu_r]$. Define the total-linking homomorphism $\varphi:H_1(X;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$ by $\varphi(\sum_i m_i[\mu_i])=\sum_i m_i$. If a smooth oriented loop $J\subset X$ is transverse to the interior of $F$, define its signed intersection number $J\cdot F$ by counting $+1$ when $J$ crosses from the negative to the positive side of the oriented normal of $F$ and $-1$ for the reverse crossing. Then $J\cdot F=\varphi([J])$.

claim: Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link in the oriented $3$-sphere, and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $L$. For disjoint oriented embedded circles $C,D\subset S^3$, define $\operatorname{lk}(C,D)$ as the coefficient of the positive meridian of $D$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus D;\mathbb Z)$, and extend it bilinearly to finite integral sums of oriented circles. This linking number is symmetric on disjoint circle cycles. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. The positive push-off $x^+$ of such a representative is a sufficiently small copy in the positive normal direction determined by the ambient and surface orientations. For representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between $x^+$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off level, and is bilinear. Hence it defines the positive-push Seifert pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$.

claim:
Assume full AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty smooth oriented link with $r$ components, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented spanning surface of genus $g$, and let $F'$ be obtained by choosing an embedded solid cylinder $[0,1]\times D^2$ that meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks and lies on the same local side at both disks, then replacing those disks by the cylinder's lateral annulus with the compatible orientation. This surgery preserves $L$. Put $m=2g+r-1$, choose an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ represented away from the two end disks, and let $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix. The surviving classes of that basis extend by two classes to an integral basis of $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$, and for some column vectors $x,y\in\mathbb Z^m$ and integer $z$, the new Seifert matrix is one of
$$
\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$

claim:
Assume full AC. For a knot Seifert surface $F$ with Seifert matrix $V$, the function $q_F(x)=x^TVx\pmod2$ is well-defined on $H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)$ and satisfies
$$q_F(x+y)=q_F(x)+q_F(y)+x\cdot_F y.$$
Its polarization is nondegenerate. For any symplectic basis $(a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g)$, the sum $\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)$ is independent of that basis. It is unchanged by either elementary Seifert enlargement, so it depends only on the knot.

claim:

$$H_\omega=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T$$
is singular if and only if the normalized knot Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ vanishes at $\omega$.

claim:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice for knot Seifert pairings. Let $G_{\mathbb Q}$ be the rational Witt group of finite-dimensional even-dimensional nonsingular symmetric rational forms equipped with an invertible isometry $T$ for which $I-T$ is invertible, modulo metabolic $T$-invariant subspaces, and let $G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the integral algebraic concordance group of Seifert lattices. The rational algebraic concordance classification due to Levine and the integral classification completed by Stoltzfus identify each of these abelian groups, as an abstract group, with
$$
\mathbb Z^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}\oplus(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{(\mathbb N)}.
$$
Here $A^{(\mathbb N)}$ denotes the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of the abelian group $A$; the statement does not identify Levine's rational classification with the distinct integral group or claim that their defining objects are the same.

claim: Let $G$ be a toroidal grid representing a knot, and use the three differentials defined by the grid-complex algorithm. For any fixed source and target states, every non-annular composite of two counted rectangles has exactly two ordered rectangle decompositions; the two decompositions have equal $O$-monomial weights and are either both counted or both excluded in each mode. Returning composites consist of thin annuli, one horizontal annulus for each row and one vertical annulus for each column. Every such annulus contains one $X$ and one $O$, so it is excluded in tilde and associated-graded minus modes. In the full filtered minus mode, each horizontal annulus contributes the variable of its unique $O$-marking, and each vertical annulus contributes the variable of its unique $O$-marking; every $O$-variable occurs once in each family and therefore twice in total. Thus all returning terms cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Every counted rectangle term has Maslov degree $-1$ and lowers Alexander filtration by exactly the number of $X$-markings in its interior; the modes excluding $X$ preserve Alexander grading.

claim:
Let $G$ be a toroidal grid representing one oriented knot, and let $\partial^-$ be the full filtered minus differential over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$. Call $O_i$ and $O_j$ consecutive when the $X$-marking in the row of $O_i$ lies in the column of $O_j$. Let $X_\ell$ be that marking and define the module map
$$H_\ell(\mathbf x)=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{r\in\operatorname{Rect}^{\circ}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\\X_\ell\in\operatorname{Int}(r)}}\left(\prod_{a=1}^{n}U_a^{O_a(r)}\right)\mathbf y.$$
Then $\partial^-H_\ell+H_\ell\partial^-=(U_i+U_j)\operatorname{id}$. The map $H_\ell$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not raise the Alexander filtration. Consequently multiplication by any two variables $U_i,U_j$ is filtered chain homotopic, since the consecutive relation follows the single cycle of the knot grid.

claim:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$. On a movie with one unaffected circle, birth a disjoint circle and then cap that same circle by a death. The composite operator is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\epsilon} \mathcal A,
$$
which is zero and therefore is not the identity, even after allowing multiplication by an overall sign.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon}"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

The movie is a cylinder on the original circle disjoint union a born-and-capped sphere; the diagram specifies the local birth and death sequence and is not used as a proof.

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$, with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$ for smooth oriented knots $K_0,K_1$. claim:
Work over $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ chain complex with Maslov grading $M$ and bifiltration coordinates $(i,j)$. Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. Define
$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

claim:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

claim: Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be the finite-rank free $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ knot Floer complex of a smooth oriented knot, with its Maslov grading, algebraic filtration $i$, Alexander filtration $j$, and weighted filtration $F_t=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j$ for a fixed $t\in[0,2]$. Assume its total homology is $\Lambda$ generated in Maslov grading zero. Then the filtered graded complex $(C,F_t)$ admits a filtered direct-sum decomposition $C=T\oplus A$, where $T=\Lambda\alpha$, $\partial\alpha=0$, $\alpha$ represents the normalized homology generator at filtration $\nu_t(C)$, and $A$ is acyclic as a graded complex. In the t-modified complex, the non-torsion tower from $T$ has maximal grading $-2\nu_t(C)$; hence this maximum equals the cycle-minimax definition of $\Upsilon_K(t)$.

claim:
Let $G$ be an $n\times n$ toroidal grid diagram representing a knot. Let $GC^-(G)$ be the finite grid complex over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$ with its Maslov grading $M$ and Alexander filtration $A$. Form the diagonal quotient
$$ D_G=GC^-(G)/(U_1-U_2,\ldots,U_1-U_n), $$
regarded as a finitely generated $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex with $U=U_1=\cdots=U_n$.

For a finitely generated Maslov-graded, Alexander-filtered complex $D$ over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with a fixed finite homogeneous basis, its $t$-modified complex for $t\in[0,2]$ is the free $\mathcal R$-module on that basis, where $\mathcal R$ is the ring of formal $\mathbb F_2$-series $\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ with support $A\subset[0,\infty)$ such that every nonempty subset of $A$ has a least element. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $\operatorname{gr}_t(x)=M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$; this action lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. The formula $M-tA$ is specified on the chosen polynomial generators. On Laurent translates, the extended grading is $M-t(j-i)$, with $v$ lowering both filtration coordinates by $1/2$. If
$$ \partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y, $$
then the modified differential is
$$ \partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y. $$
A homogeneous homology class is **non-torsion** if no nonzero element of $\mathcal R$ annihilates it. For $0\le t\le1$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ to be the maximum $t$-grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D_G^t)$. For $1<t\le2$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$. This is the grid convention compared with the original cycle-minimax invariant.

claim:
Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

claim:
Assume countable choice. Let $(B,G,R)$ be a dualizable framed handle link and
let $X(B,G,R)$ be its associated handlebody. There are finite sequences of
handle slides and cancellations, first sliding $G$ over $B$ and cancelling
the $1$-handle $R$ with the $2$-handle $B$, and then using the reversed roles,
that leave single $0$-framed attaching knots $K_G$ and $K_B$, respectively.
There are diffeomorphisms
$$
X(B,G,R)\cong X_0(K_G)\cong X_0(K_B).
$$
